## Literature Review Report: Competing and Missing Work for OntoCoDec

Below is a systematic review across all 10 search queries, with findings organized by relevance and potential threat level to the OntoCoDec proposal.

---

### 1. Constrained Decoding for Information Extraction (2025–2026)

**Directly relevant papers the proposal may have missed:**

**Grammar-Constrained Decoding for Structured IE (January 2025, Frontiers in AI / PMC:PMC11747381)**
Published in *Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence*, this empirical study applies grammar-constrained decoding to fine-tuned generative models for clinical trial IE. It reports F1 improvements of 0.351–0.425 points over unconstrained baselines, and explicitly discusses the tradeoffs between grammar-based constraints, pointer generators, and low-resource settings. This is a direct domain application of grammar-constrained decoding to IE. The proposal should cite this.

**Lazy-k Decoding: Constrained Decoding for Information Extraction (EMNLP 2023, with 2025 follow-up)**
The foundational paper ([ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.416/), arXiv:2312.03367) combines probabilistic token-classification models with constrained decoding for IE. A 2025 analysis cites it as a baseline, noting that in IE, "unconstrained decoding F1 often trails the constrained variant by 5–13 absolute points." If OntoCoDec does not cite Lazy-k, this is a significant omission.

**Constrained Decoding with Speculative Lookaheads (NAACL 2025)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.239/) / arXiv:2412.10418. Amazon Science paper presenting CDSL, which applies speculative decoding to accelerate lookahead-heuristic constrained decoding. Achieves 2.2x–12.15x speedup over prior constrained decoding with lookahead (CDLH). Relevant because OntoCoDec's logit masking at every step incurs overhead that this line of work addresses.

**The Hidden Cost of Structure: How Constrained Decoding Affects Language Model Performance (RANLP 2025)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.ranlp-1.124/) — Investigates 11 models across multiple benchmarks. Key finding: constrained decoding forces models away from their preferred distributions, causing measurable quality degradation ("alignment tax"). This is a critical negative result the proposal should address to pre-empt reviewers asking "does logit masking hurt extraction quality?"

**From Hallucination to Structure Snowballing: The Alignment Tax of Constrained Decoding in LLM Reflection (April 2026)**
[arXiv:2604.06066](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.06066) — Extends the "alignment tax" finding to agentic reflection workflows. Directly challenges the premise that constrained decoding is uniformly beneficial.

**Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars (2026, OpenReview)**
[OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=7Sph4KyeYO) — Extends constrained decoding to diffusion-based LLMs by reducing to formal language operations. Not directly competing for IE but shows the field is moving beyond autoregressive-only constrained decoding.

**Awesome-LLM-Constrained-Decoding (GitHub, actively maintained)**
[GitHub](https://github.com/Saibo-creator/Awesome-LLM-Constrained-Decoding) — A curated paper list. The proposal authors should check this for any overlooked papers in the space.

---

### 2. Ontology-Constrained LLM Knowledge Extraction (2025–2026)

**ODKE+: Ontology-Guided Open-Domain Knowledge Extraction with LLMs (September 2025)**
[arXiv:2509.04696](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.04696) — Deployed in production at Apple since May 2025. Dynamically generates ontology snippets per entity type to align LLM extractions with schema constraints. Processes 9M Wikipedia pages; 98.8% precision; 19M facts ingested. This is a **major competing system** for OntoCoDec — it does ontology-guided extraction at scale using LLMs, though it uses prompting rather than decoding-time logit masking. The proposal almost certainly needs to address this.

**OntoKG: Ontology-Oriented Knowledge Graph Construction (April 2026)**
[arXiv:2604.02618](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02618v1) — Ontology-oriented KG construction with LLM-guided extraction. Similar motivation to OntoCoDec but prompt-based.

**OntoGPT (2025, Environmental Evidence journal)**
[Springer](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13750-026-00381-0) — Combines LLMs with ontologies for structured IE, achieving 65% agreement with human reviewers. Uses ontology-grounded prompting. Directly comparable baseline for OntoCoDec's accuracy claims.

**LLM-empowered Knowledge Graph Construction: A Survey (October 2025)**
[arXiv:2510.20345](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20345v1) — Comprehensive survey covering static-schema IE and ontology-driven LLM extraction. OntoCoDec should cite this survey to contextualize its contributions.

**LLM-Driven Ontology Construction for Enterprise Knowledge Graphs (February 2026)**
[arXiv:2602.01276](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.01276v1) — Discusses LLM-based ontology-driven KG construction for enterprises.

**Data, Evaluation Framework and Ontology-guided LLM... (EACL 2026 Findings)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-eacl.130.pdf) — Appears directly in the same space; the title was cut off but the venue (EACL 2026 Findings) makes this a **high priority to read** — it may be a direct competitor.

**Ontology-conformal Recognition of Materials Entities Using Language Models (May 2025, Nature Scientific Reports)**
[Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-03619-y) — Benchmarks foundation LLMs on ontology-constrained NER. Key finding: task-specific models significantly outperform general LLMs on ontology-constrained NER. Relevant for OntoCoDec's claims about zero-shot or few-shot performance.

---

### 3. Schema-Guided Information Extraction with LLMs (2025–2026)

**PARSE: LLM Driven Schema Optimization for Reliable Entity Extraction (EMNLP 2025 Industry Track)**
[arXiv:2510.08623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08623) / [Amazon Science](https://www.amazon.science/publications/parse-llm-driven-schema-optimization-for-reliable-entity-extraction) — Specifically criticizes approaches that use JSON schemas as static contracts (which OntoCoDec's compiled constraint specs resemble). PARSE proposes dynamic schema optimization via an ARCHITECT module before extraction. This is a **direct methodological critique** of the approach OntoCoDec takes, and the proposal must engage with it.

**SLOT: Structuring the Output of Large Language Models (EMNLP 2025 Industry)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-industry.32.pdf) — An industry approach to structured LLM output. Relevant comparison point.

**LLM-based Schema-Guided Extraction and Validation of Missing-Person Intelligence (April 2026)**
[arXiv:2604.06571](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06571) — Schema-guided extraction with validation for heterogeneous data. Recent applied work in the same space.

**Generating Structured Outputs from Language Models: Benchmark and Studies (January 2025)**
[arXiv:2501.10868](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.10868v1) — Benchmarks constrained decoding approaches for structured output across efficiency, coverage, and quality. If OntoCoDec doesn't cite this benchmark paper, reviewers may flag it.

---

### 4. Type Constraints for Relation Extraction at Decoding Time (2025–2026)

**DocRE-TCGL: Document-Level Relation Extraction with Entity Type Constraints (2025, Neural Networks / ScienceDirect)**
[ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0893608025013504) — The paper the proposal references. Confirmed real. Claims to be "the first time entity type constraints are used to capture relation correlations to solve both long-tail and multi-label problems in DocRE." Uses a Type-Constrained Graph (TCG) globally and a Type-Constrained Loss (TCL) locally — but this is a **training-time** approach, not decoding-time. Performance gains: up to 6.26% on long-tail and 4.91% on multi-label setups. The proposal's framing should clearly distinguish OntoCoDec's decoding-time enforcement from DocRE-TCGL's training-time constraint learning.

**SH-ETRs: Learning Soft-Hard Rules with Entity Type Constraints for Document-Level RE (September 2025)**
[ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0957417425032750) — A second training-time type-constraint approach for DocRE published in *Expert Systems with Applications*. F1 of 74.39, IgnF1 of 67.43 across three datasets. State-of-the-art at time of publication. The proposal likely **overlooked this** if it was not available at submission time, but it is now a required comparison.

**Context-aware Inductive KGC with Latent Type Constraints and Subgraph Reasoning (October 2024 / updated 2025)**
[arXiv:2410.16803](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.16803) — CATS, with a Type-Aware Reasoning module that evaluates whether candidate entities conform to implicit type constraints of relations. Works in KGC rather than IE, but the mechanism is closely analogous.

---

### 5. Structured Output LLM Information Extraction (2025–2026)

The structured output landscape has changed rapidly. Key facts OntoCoDec's related work section may understate:

- **XGrammar** (arXiv:2411.15100) is now the default backend for vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and TensorRT-LLM as of March 2026, achieving under 40 microseconds per token. **XGrammar-2** was released May 2026.
- **llguidance** (Microsoft/guidance-ai) provides per-token CFG-based constraint calculation as an alternative.
- **Anthropic added constrained decoding** for Claude in November 2025 (GA early 2026).
- These infrastructure developments mean OntoCoDec's logit-masking mechanism is no longer novel at the infrastructure level — its novelty must come from the **ontology compilation and semantic constraint specification**, not the logit masking mechanism itself.

**Generating Structured Outputs from Language Models: Benchmark and Studies (2025)**
[arXiv:2501.10868](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.10868v1) — Comprehensive benchmark of structured output approaches.

---

### 6. GoLLIE (ICLR 2024) — Verification

**Confirmed real and correctly positioned.** GoLLIE ([OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=Y3wpuxd7u9), arXiv:2310.03668, ICLR 2024 conference paper) fine-tunes an LLM to follow annotation guidelines for zero-shot IE. Authors: Sainz, García-Ferrero, Agerri, Lopez de Lacalle, Rigau, Agirre (HiTZ, University of the Basque Country). The key distinction from OntoCoDec is that GoLLIE enforces guideline compliance via fine-tuning, not decoding-time constraints. The proposal's framing of GoLLIE as a training-time baseline appears correct.

---

### 7. SciDC: Scientific Knowledge-Driven Decoding Constraints (April 2026) — Verification

**Confirmed real and highly relevant.** [arXiv:2604.06603](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06603), submitted April 8, 2026. Authors: Maotian Ma, Zheni Zeng, Zhenghao Liu, Yukun Yan. Converts domain knowledge into "multi-layered, standardized rules" that constrain LLM generation for scientific tasks (industrial formulation design, clinical tumor diagnosis, retrosynthesis planning). Average 12% accuracy improvement over vanilla generation. This is **very close to OntoCoDec's approach** — it compiles knowledge into decoding-time constraints — but for scientific correctness rather than IE ontology compliance. The proposal must cite and differentiate from SciDC.

---

### 8. DocRE-TCGL — Verification

**Confirmed real** (see Section 4 above). Training-time approach, not decoding-time. The distinction is important for the proposal.

---

### 9. Grammar-Constrained Decoding for NER/RE (2026)

**No 2026 papers found that are specifically grammar-constrained decoding for NER/RE** beyond what was covered in Sections 1 and 4. The most recent grammar-constrained IE work remains:

- Geng et al. (EMNLP 2023), "Grammar-Constrained Decoding for Structured NLP Tasks without Finetuning" [arXiv:2305.13971](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.13971v6)
- The clinical trial IE application (January 2025)

**IterGen (ICLR 2025)** [arXiv:2410.07295](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07295) is notable: it adds **backtracking** to grammar-guided generation by tracking symbol-to-position mappings and KV-cache state. Demonstrated on SQL and Vega-Lite generation. OntoCoDec's logit-masking approach is forward-only; IterGen's backtracking could be a reviewer concern (what happens when the model generates a valid-but-wrong entity type that forecloses valid continuations?).

**Dialogue Ontology RE via Constrained Chain-of-Thought Decoding (SIGDIAL 2024 / updated March 2025)**
[arXiv:2408.02361](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02361) — Constrains CoT decoding to terms and relation types from the target ontology for task-oriented dialogue. This is a **direct conceptual competitor**: it enforces ontology-specified relation types at generation time. The proposal almost certainly overlooked this paper if it was framed as a 2024 publication.

---

### 10. Logit Masking for Semantic Constraints (2025–2026)

**LOGIC: Logit-Space Integration for Speech LLMs (January 2026)**
[arXiv:2601.15397](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15397v1) — Applies logit-space biasing to constrain entity types in speech recognition. While the domain is speech, the mechanism (logit-space entity-type enforcement) is essentially what OntoCoDec does for text IE.

**ICLR 2025 SMC for Semantic Parsing paper** — Uses per-token logit masking to enforce CFG constraints, then uses Sequential Monte Carlo to handle constraints that cannot be efficiently encoded in logit masks. Key insight: logit masks cannot capture all semantically valid constraints; SMC is needed for the remainder. This is a **theoretical gap** the proposal should acknowledge.

**Logically Consistent Language Models via Neuro-Symbolic Integration (ICLR 2025 submission)**
[OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=7PGluppo4k) — Trains models to be consistent with external facts and rules via a neuro-symbolic loss. Training-time rather than decoding-time, but directly relevant background.

---

## "Conversational Control with Ontologies for Large Language Models: A Lightweight Framework for Constrained Generation"

**arXiv ID:** 2604.04450
**Submitted:** April 6, 2026
**Authors:** Barbara Gendron, Gaël Guibon, Mathieu d'Aquin

### Overview

This work proposes an end-to-end method to obtain modular and explainable control over LLM outputs through ontological definitions of aspects related to the conversation. Key aspects are modeled and used as constraints; the LLM is then further fine-tuned to generate content accordingly.

### Motivation

Conversational agents based on Large Language Models have recently emerged as powerful tools for human-computer interaction. Nevertheless, their black-box nature implies challenges in predictability and a lack of personalization, both of which can be addressed by controlled generation.

### Methodology & Validation

The approach is validated by exploring two tasks that tackle two key conversational aspects: the English proficiency level and the polarity profile of the content. Using a hybrid fine-tuning procedure on seven state-of-the-art, open-weight conversational LLMs, the method consistently outperforms pre-trained baselines, even on smaller models.

The paper is available on arXiv at https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.04450

## Literature Review Report: Competing and Missing Work for OntoCoDec

Below is a systematic review across all 10 search queries, with findings organized by relevance and potential threat level to the OntoCoDec proposal.

---

### 1. Constrained Decoding for Information Extraction (2025–2026)

**Directly relevant papers the proposal may have missed:**

**Grammar-Constrained Decoding for Structured IE (January 2025, Frontiers in AI / PMC:PMC11747381)**
Published in *Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence*, this empirical study applies grammar-constrained decoding to fine-tuned generative models for clinical trial IE. It reports F1 improvements of 0.351–0.425 points over unconstrained baselines, and explicitly discusses the tradeoffs between grammar-based constraints, pointer generators, and low-resource settings. This is a direct domain application of grammar-constrained decoding to IE. The proposal should cite this.

**Lazy-k Decoding: Constrained Decoding for Information Extraction (EMNLP 2023, with 2025 follow-up)**
The foundational paper ([ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.416/), arXiv:2312.03367) combines probabilistic token-classification models with constrained decoding for IE. A 2025 analysis cites it as a baseline, noting that in IE, "unconstrained decoding F1 often trails the constrained variant by 5–13 absolute points." If OntoCoDec does not cite Lazy-k, this is a significant omission.

**Constrained Decoding with Speculative Lookaheads (NAACL 2025)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-long.239/) / arXiv:2412.10418. Amazon Science paper presenting CDSL, which applies speculative decoding to accelerate lookahead-heuristic constrained decoding. Achieves 2.2x–12.15x speedup over prior constrained decoding with lookahead (CDLH). Relevant because OntoCoDec's logit masking at every step incurs overhead that this line of work addresses.

**The Hidden Cost of Structure: How Constrained Decoding Affects Language Model Performance (RANLP 2025)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.ranlp-1.124/) — Investigates 11 models across multiple benchmarks. Key finding: constrained decoding forces models away from their preferred distributions, causing measurable quality degradation ("alignment tax"). This is a critical negative result the proposal should address to pre-empt reviewers asking "does logit masking hurt extraction quality?"

**From Hallucination to Structure Snowballing: The Alignment Tax of Constrained Decoding in LLM Reflection (April 2026)**
[arXiv:2604.06066](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.06066) — Extends the "alignment tax" finding to agentic reflection workflows. Directly challenges the premise that constrained decoding is uniformly beneficial.

**Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars (2026, OpenReview)**
[OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=7Sph4KyeYO) — Extends constrained decoding to diffusion-based LLMs by reducing to formal language operations. Not directly competing for IE but shows the field is moving beyond autoregressive-only constrained decoding.

**Awesome-LLM-Constrained-Decoding (GitHub, actively maintained)**
[GitHub](https://github.com/Saibo-creator/Awesome-LLM-Constrained-Decoding) — A curated paper list. The proposal authors should check this for any overlooked papers in the space.

---

### 2. Ontology-Constrained LLM Knowledge Extraction (2025–2026)

**ODKE+: Ontology-Guided Open-Domain Knowledge Extraction with LLMs (September 2025)**
[arXiv:2509.04696](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.04696) — Deployed in production at Apple since May 2025. Dynamically generates ontology snippets per entity type to align LLM extractions with schema constraints. Processes 9M Wikipedia pages; 98.8% precision; 19M facts ingested. This is a **major competing system** for OntoCoDec — it does ontology-guided extraction at scale using LLMs, though it uses prompting rather than decoding-time logit masking. The proposal almost certainly needs to address this.

**OntoKG: Ontology-Oriented Knowledge Graph Construction (April 2026)**
[arXiv:2604.02618](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02618v1) — Ontology-oriented KG construction with LLM-guided extraction. Similar motivation to OntoCoDec but prompt-based.

**OntoGPT (2025, Environmental Evidence journal)**
[Springer](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13750-026-00381-0) — Combines LLMs with ontologies for structured IE, achieving 65% agreement with human reviewers. Uses ontology-grounded prompting. Directly comparable baseline for OntoCoDec's accuracy claims.

**LLM-empowered Knowledge Graph Construction: A Survey (October 2025)**
[arXiv:2510.20345](https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20345v1) — Comprehensive survey covering static-schema IE and ontology-driven LLM extraction. OntoCoDec should cite this survey to contextualize its contributions.

**LLM-Driven Ontology Construction for Enterprise Knowledge Graphs (February 2026)**
[arXiv:2602.01276](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.01276v1) — Discusses LLM-based ontology-driven KG construction for enterprises.

**Data, Evaluation Framework and Ontology-guided LLM... (EACL 2026 Findings)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-eacl.130.pdf) — Appears directly in the same space; the title was cut off but the venue (EACL 2026 Findings) makes this a **high priority to read** — it may be a direct competitor.

**Ontology-conformal Recognition of Materials Entities Using Language Models (May 2025, Nature Scientific Reports)**
[Nature](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-03619-y) — Benchmarks foundation LLMs on ontology-constrained NER. Key finding: task-specific models significantly outperform general LLMs on ontology-constrained NER. Relevant for OntoCoDec's claims about zero-shot or few-shot performance.

---

### 3. Schema-Guided Information Extraction with LLMs (2025–2026)

**PARSE: LLM Driven Schema Optimization for Reliable Entity Extraction (EMNLP 2025 Industry Track)**
[arXiv:2510.08623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.08623) / [Amazon Science](https://www.amazon.science/publications/parse-llm-driven-schema-optimization-for-reliable-entity-extraction) — Specifically criticizes approaches that use JSON schemas as static contracts (which OntoCoDec's compiled constraint specs resemble). PARSE proposes dynamic schema optimization via an ARCHITECT module before extraction. This is a **direct methodological critique** of the approach OntoCoDec takes, and the proposal must engage with it.

**SLOT: Structuring the Output of Large Language Models (EMNLP 2025 Industry)**
[ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-industry.32.pdf) — An industry approach to structured LLM output. Relevant comparison point.

**LLM-based Schema-Guided Extraction and Validation of Missing-Person Intelligence (April 2026)**
[arXiv:2604.06571](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06571) — Schema-guided extraction with validation for heterogeneous data. Recent applied work in the same space.

**Generating Structured Outputs from Language Models: Benchmark and Studies (January 2025)**
[arXiv:2501.10868](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.10868v1) — Benchmarks constrained decoding approaches for structured output across efficiency, coverage, and quality. If OntoCoDec doesn't cite this benchmark paper, reviewers may flag it.

---

### 4. Type Constraints for Relation Extraction at Decoding Time (2025–2026)

**DocRE-TCGL: Document-Level Relation Extraction with Entity Type Constraints (2025, Neural Networks / ScienceDirect)**
[ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0893608025013504) — The paper the proposal references. Confirmed real. Claims to be "the first time entity type constraints are used to capture relation correlations to solve both long-tail and multi-label problems in DocRE." Uses a Type-Constrained Graph (TCG) globally and a Type-Constrained Loss (TCL) locally — but this is a **training-time** approach, not decoding-time. Performance gains: up to 6.26% on long-tail and 4.91% on multi-label setups. The proposal's framing should clearly distinguish OntoCoDec's decoding-time enforcement from DocRE-TCGL's training-time constraint learning.

**SH-ETRs: Learning Soft-Hard Rules with Entity Type Constraints for Document-Level RE (September 2025)**
[ScienceDirect](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0957417425032750) — A second training-time type-constraint approach for DocRE published in *Expert Systems with Applications*. F1 of 74.39, IgnF1 of 67.43 across three datasets. State-of-the-art at time of publication. The proposal likely **overlooked this** if it was not available at submission time, but it is now a required comparison.

**Context-aware Inductive KGC with Latent Type Constraints and Subgraph Reasoning (October 2024 / updated 2025)**
[arXiv:2410.16803](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.16803) — CATS, with a Type-Aware Reasoning module that evaluates whether candidate entities conform to implicit type constraints of relations. Works in KGC rather than IE, but the mechanism is closely analogous.

---

### 5. Structured Output LLM Information Extraction (2025–2026)

The structured output landscape has changed rapidly. Key facts OntoCoDec's related work section may understate:

- **XGrammar** (arXiv:2411.15100) is now the default backend for vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, and TensorRT-LLM as of March 2026, achieving under 40 microseconds per token. **XGrammar-2** was released May 2026.
- **llguidance** (Microsoft/guidance-ai) provides per-token CFG-based constraint calculation as an alternative.
- **Anthropic added constrained decoding** for Claude in November 2025 (GA early 2026).
- These infrastructure developments mean OntoCoDec's logit-masking mechanism is no longer novel at the infrastructure level — its novelty must come from the **ontology compilation and semantic constraint specification**, not the logit masking mechanism itself.

**Generating Structured Outputs from Language Models: Benchmark and Studies (2025)**
[arXiv:2501.10868](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.10868v1) — Comprehensive benchmark of structured output approaches.

---

### 6. GoLLIE (ICLR 2024) — Verification

**Confirmed real and correctly positioned.** GoLLIE ([OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=Y3wpuxd7u9), arXiv:2310.03668, ICLR 2024 conference paper) fine-tunes an LLM to follow annotation guidelines for zero-shot IE. Authors: Sainz, García-Ferrero, Agerri, Lopez de Lacalle, Rigau, Agirre (HiTZ, University of the Basque Country). The key distinction from OntoCoDec is that GoLLIE enforces guideline compliance via fine-tuning, not decoding-time constraints. The proposal's framing of GoLLIE as a training-time baseline appears correct.

---

### 7. SciDC: Scientific Knowledge-Driven Decoding Constraints (April 2026) — Verification

**Confirmed real and highly relevant.** [arXiv:2604.06603](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.06603), submitted April 8, 2026. Authors: Maotian Ma, Zheni Zeng, Zhenghao Liu, Yukun Yan. Converts domain knowledge into "multi-layered, standardized rules" that constrain LLM generation for scientific tasks (industrial formulation design, clinical tumor diagnosis, retrosynthesis planning). Average 12% accuracy improvement over vanilla generation. This is **very close to OntoCoDec's approach** — it compiles knowledge into decoding-time constraints — but for scientific correctness rather than IE ontology compliance. The proposal must cite and differentiate from SciDC.

---

### 8. DocRE-TCGL — Verification

**Confirmed real** (see Section 4 above). Training-time approach, not decoding-time. The distinction is important for the proposal.

---

### 9. Grammar-Constrained Decoding for NER/RE (2026)

**No 2026 papers found that are specifically grammar-constrained decoding for NER/RE** beyond what was covered in Sections 1 and 4. The most recent grammar-constrained IE work remains:

- Geng et al. (EMNLP 2023), "Grammar-Constrained Decoding for Structured NLP Tasks without Finetuning" [arXiv:2305.13971](https://arxiv.org/html/2305.13971v6)
- The clinical trial IE application (January 2025)

**IterGen (ICLR 2025)** [arXiv:2410.07295](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07295) is notable: it adds **backtracking** to grammar-guided generation by tracking symbol-to-position mappings and KV-cache state. Demonstrated on SQL and Vega-Lite generation. OntoCoDec's logit-masking approach is forward-only; IterGen's backtracking could be a reviewer concern (what happens when the model generates a valid-but-wrong entity type that forecloses valid continuations?).

**Dialogue Ontology RE via Constrained Chain-of-Thought Decoding (SIGDIAL 2024 / updated March 2025)**
[arXiv:2408.02361](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02361) — Constrains CoT decoding to terms and relation types from the target ontology for task-oriented dialogue. This is a **direct conceptual competitor**: it enforces ontology-specified relation types at generation time. The proposal almost certainly overlooked this paper if it was framed as a 2024 publication.

---

### 10. Logit Masking for Semantic Constraints (2025–2026)

**LOGIC: Logit-Space Integration for Speech LLMs (January 2026)**
[arXiv:2601.15397](https://arxiv.org/html/2601.15397v1) — Applies logit-space biasing to constrain entity types in speech recognition. While the domain is speech, the mechanism (logit-space entity-type enforcement) is essentially what OntoCoDec does for text IE.

**ICLR 2025 SMC for Semantic Parsing paper** — Uses per-token logit masking to enforce CFG constraints, then uses Sequential Monte Carlo to handle constraints that cannot be efficiently encoded in logit masks. Key insight: logit masks cannot capture all semantically valid constraints; SMC is needed for the remainder. This is a **theoretical gap** the proposal should acknowledge.

**Logically Consistent Language Models via Neuro-Symbolic Integration (ICLR 2025 submission)**
[OpenReview](https://openreview.net/forum?id=7PGluppo4k) — Trains models to be consistent with external facts and rules via a neuro-symbolic loss. Training-time rather than decoding-time, but directly relevant background.

---

## Summary: Highest-Priority Missing/Competing Works

The following are the works most likely to concern reviewers if absent from OntoCoDec's related work section:

I found the paper you're looking for! Here's a summary of the search results:

## Paper: "Dialogue Ontology Relation Extraction via Constrained Chain-of-Thought Decoding"

**Publication Details:**
- arXiv ID: 2408.02361, accepted to appear at SIGDIAL 2024
- Proceedings of the 25th Annual Meeting of the Special Interest Group on Discourse and Dialogue, pages 370–384, Kyoto, Japan

**Authors:**
Renato Vukovic, David Arps, Carel van Niekerk, Benjamin Matthias Ruppik, Hsien-chin Lin, Michael Heck, and Milica Gasic

**Main Contribution:**
The paper adapts Chain-of-Thought (CoT) decoding, recently developed for reasoning problems, to generative relation extraction, generating multiple branches in the decoding space and selecting the relations based on a confidence threshold.

**Key Research Problem:**
State-of-the-art task-oriented dialogue systems typically rely on task-specific ontologies, but the majority of task-oriented dialogue data comes without ontology and annotation, with such ontologies normally built manually, limiting the application of specialised systems.

**Approach:**
By constraining the decoding to ontology terms and relations, the authors aim to decrease the risk of hallucination.

This paper by Ravikumar, Ibrahim, and Batista-Navarro investigates how the choice of output format influences the performance of fine-tuned large language models on information extraction tasks. It was presented at the 19th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL 2026) in Rabat, Morocco in March 2026.

Based on over 280 experiments spanning multiple benchmarks, models and formats, the authors found that output formatting is a critical yet largely overlooked hyperparameter.

The authors further observe that no single format consistently dominates across settings, and the optimal choice depends on factors like model family and dataset characteristics.

The paper appears in the ACL Anthology at pages 5498-5513 and demonstrates that informationally equivalent output formats can produce substantial performance variation, highlighting the need to treat output formatting as a key factor in building accurate and reliable information extraction systems.

## UniNER (UniversalNER)

UniNER demonstrates how ChatGPT can be distilled into much smaller UniversalNER models for open NER. The dataset comprises 45,889 input-output pairs, encompassing 240,725 entities and 13,020 distinct entity types.

### Benchmark
The Universal NER benchmark encompasses 43 NER datasets across 9 domains, including general, biomedical, clinical, STEM, programming, social media, law, finance, and transportation domains.

### Performance (SOTA Results)
With a tiny fraction of parameters, UniversalNER not only acquires ChatGPT's capability in recognizing arbitrary entity types, but also outperforms its NER accuracy by 7-9 absolute F1 points in average. UniversalNER even outperforms by a large margin state-of-the-art multi-task instruction-tuned systems such as InstructUIE, which uses supervised NER examples.

## Universal NER (UNER) - Multilingual Benchmark

Note: There's also a separate "Universal NER" (UNER) project published at NAACL 2024. Universal NER (UNER) is an open, community-driven project to develop gold-standard NER benchmarks in many languages, with UNER v1 containing 19 datasets annotated with named entities in a cross-lingual consistent schema across 13 diverse languages.

The UniNER model has been adopted in recent frameworks for information extraction applications, demonstrating its practical utility in 2024-2025 NER systems.

Now I have extensive data from all three research agents and my own searches. Let me synthesize all findings and produce my review.

## Summary of Findings

### Reference Verification
All key references verified as real:
- IterGen (ICLR 2025) ✓
- Synchromesh (ICLR 2022) ✓ 
- LLM+ASP (arXiv 2508.12611, ICLP 2025) ✓ - SciERC 35.37% RE F1 confirmed
- BoostCD/BoostIE (EMNLP 2025) ✓


- ODKE+ (Apple, Sep 2025) ✓ - 98.8% precision confirmed
- The Format Tax (arXiv Apr 2026) ✓
- CRANE (ICML 2025) ✓ - TC⁰ confirmed
- EnriCo (arXiv Apr 2024) ✓ - preprint, no confirmed major venue
- DocRE-TCGL ✓
- Ru-LLM (NLPCC 2025) ✓
- Re2-DocRED (EACL 2026) ✓
- SciD

Continuing to verify the remaining references from the paper.

Looking at the EMNLP 2026 deadline — May 25th gives us about two weeks to finalize the submission. For the violation rate claim, there's no existing published measurement of ontology type violations specifically, which actually supports the novelty of what we're proposing. The general IE error landscape shows violations are definitely a real problem — GPT-4 class models hit around 12% invalid extraction rates, and complex schema tasks see even worse performance. Constrained decoding helps narrow this gap by 5-13 F1 points on IE tasks, so the >5% violation threshold we're using seems reasonable even if it hasn't been formally proven yet.

The infrastructure checks all look solid — vLLM's LogitsProcessor API works as expected, XGrammar-2's masking and tag dispatch are confirmed, and that Qwen3 bug we hit is fixed in vLLM 0.9.0. The Structure Snowballing effect is real too, with Qwen3-8B's performance dropping from 50% down to 38% when constrained decoding kicks in. Now I'm reviewing what related work we've already covered — IterGen, Synchromesh, BoostCD/BoostIE, LLM+ASP, ODKE+, GoLLIE, and DocRE-TCGL are all in there, so I need to identify what gaps remain in the landscape.

Looking through the expanded list of cited work, we've got solid coverage across recent approaches like XGrammar-2, Structure Snowballing, The Format Tax, and various entity/relation extraction methods like CRANE, EnriCo, and RELATE. The dialogue-related work seems to be starting to emerge as a potential gap.

I'm noticing a few additional papers that touch on related territory: there's work on constrained decoding for ontology-aligned relation extraction in dialogue systems, which is conceptually adjacent but focuses on task-oriented dialogue rather than information extraction ontologies like ACE05. There's also recent work on ontology-guided prompting for humanitarian applications that shows significant improvements in extraction quality and hallucination reduction through prompt engineering rather than decoding constraints. And there's emerging research on how output formatting itself can dramatically shift performance metrics in IE tasks.

The remaining papers I'm considering—on dynamic schema optimization, constrained decoding efficiency, and task-specific models for ontology-constrained NER—are either tangential or already covered by existing citations in the proposal. None of these gaps seem substantial enough to challenge the core novelty or claims.
